threads.body: [General] `BigInteger.longValue()` keeps only the low 64 bits rather than producing a valid truncated byte count. The out-of-range value exercised by the new test therefore exports an unrelated value (and other inputs can become negative), making this gauge inaccurate. Detect overflow with `longValueExact()` and skip or otherwise explicitly handle that compaction entry; update the test to verify the chosen behavior.
[Style] Internal implementation classes should not be declared `final` under the repository's Java style rules. Remove `final` from this class in the `.internal` package.

[General] Worth settling before this lands, since metric names are hard to change afterwards: `.bytes` repeats the `By` unit in the name, and OpenTelemetry metric naming guidance steers away from a `.total` suffix.

[Style] `cassandra.md` and every other Cassandra `desc:` end with a period.

```suggestion
            .setDescription("Bytes completed for in-flight compactions.")
            .setUnit("By")
            .ofLongs()
            .buildObserver();

    ObservableLongMeasurement totalGauge =
        meter
            .gaugeBuilder(METRIC_TOTAL)
            .setDescription("Total bytes for in-flight compactions.")
```

[General] This runs on every collection cycle, so a persistent failure logs a `WARNING` plus stack trace every interval. The engine logs the same class of per-collection failure at `FINE` (see `BeanAttributeExtractor`). Same for the overflow warning on line 135.
[Testing] This re-implements the merge lambda, so the test only verifies its own copy. Making `queryGroups` package-private and driving it with a fake `Detector` would exercise the real path.

replies.body: Replaced the hand-rolled merge with a call to the real `queryGroups()` via an anonymous `Detector`
`triggerCompaction` now accepts an `AtomicBoolean` and loops `nodetool compact` until it's cleared; `keepCompacting.set(false)` called in a `finally` block after `verifyMetrics`

threads.body: [Testing] If `nodetool compact` fails, the test still waits the full 60s and then fails with a missing-metric error rather than the nodetool output. Recording the failure and surfacing it in the assertion would make this much easier to debug.

[General] Worth a look at what actually lands in `cassandra.compaction.task_type`. `CompactionInfo.asMap()` writes this entry as `OperationType.toString()`, and `OperationType` overrides `toString()` to return its human-readable `type` field — so the values are `Compaction`, `Validation`, `Cleanup`, `Upgrade sstables`, `Secondary index build`, etc., not the enum names.

That gives a metric attribute with mixed case and embedded spaces, which is inconsistent with the rest of `experimental-cassandra.yaml`, where values are normalized (`lowercase(param(scope))` for `cassandra.operation`, `const(unavailable)` for `cassandra.status`). Lowercasing and replacing spaces with `_` would make it a stable dimension.

The unit test fixtures use `"COMPACTION"`/`"VALIDATION"`/`"ANTICOMPACTION"`, which is why this doesn't show up anywhere — using the real forms there would document the actual values.

[Testing] This assertion can't fail — `getName()` just returns `HANDLER_NAME`, so it's comparing the constant to itself. The thing actually worth pinning is that the name matches the `handler: cassandra-compaction-progress` key in `experimental-cassandra.yaml`, which only a literal catches:

```suggestion
    assertThat(new CassandraCompactionProgressHandler().getName())
        .isEqualTo("cassandra-compaction-progress");
```

With that, `HANDLER_NAME` has no remaining test usage and can become `private` too.

[Testing] The handler guards three dimension fields but this only exercises two — a null `taskType` never reaches the `continue`:

```suggestion
            asList(
                compactionEntry("COMPACTION", "ks1", "cf1", "10", "100"),
                compactionEntry(null, "ks1", "cf1", "5", "50"),
                compactionEntry("COMPACTION", null, "cf1", "5", "50"),
                compactionEntry("COMPACTION", "ks1", null, "5", "50")));
```

[Naming] `ignored` is the convention for a genuinely unused catch variable; this one is read in the loop condition and incremented, so it reads as a contradiction.

```suggestion
      for (int i = 0; i < COMPACTION_BATCHES; i++) {
```

[Testing] If `nodetool compact` fails while the container is still up, the thread returns and compaction stops for the rest of the run. The test then doesn't fail *here* — it fails 60s later inside `verifyMetrics` with a "metric not found" assertion that says nothing about compaction, and the only breadcrumb is a warning whose cause was dropped (`e.getMessage()` on the `IllegalStateException` from `execOrThrow` is just the exit-code/stdout/stderr blob).

Separately, `java.util.logging` is the odd one out here — test code in this module uses SLF4J (`TargetSystemTest`, `WeaverContainer`), as does essentially all test code in the repo, and while `jul-to-slf4j` is on the test classpath nothing installs `SLF4JBridgeHandler`, so this record bypasses logback entirely.

Minimum fix, match the parent class and keep the cause:

```java
private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(CassandraTest.class);
...
logger.warn("Background compaction failed", e);
```

Better still, make it surface: stash it in an `AtomicReference<Exception>` here and check it in `testCassandraMetrics`, so a broken `nodetool` invocation is reported as the real cause instead of a timeout.
